mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5.25% in a given month reduces near-term discount rates, lowering the present value of expected corporate cash flows and thus producing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or flat during the trigger, with no significant mean reversion detected in walk-forward tests.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in UNRATE above 6% signals labor market weakness, raising perceived equity risk and depressing short-term discounting, which drives negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in >50% of UNRATE > 6% months, or IC > 0.1 over rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: When the HOUST industrial production index exceeds 1500 for two consecutive months, it indicates accelerating demand for consumer goods, which is associated with positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: No significant return in 20 days during qualifying periods, or IC < 0.05 in out-of-sample tests.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO below 105 suggests weakening manufacturing capacity, which raises uncertainty and compresses equity valuations, producing negative 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: INDPRO declines are not associated with negative 20-day returns, or IC > 0.1 in walk-forward evaluation.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in both FEDFUNDS and GDPC1 (quarterly) indicate a dual signal of rate cuts and weak demand, jointly depressing discount rates and equity valuations, yielding negative 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are positive in >40% of such dual-signal quarters, or interaction term is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: When PAYEMS exceeds 150,000 for three consecutive months, it reflects strong labor market absorption, lowering risk aversion and supporting positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: No positive 20-day returns during qualifying periods, or IC < -0.1 in out-of-sample.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in RSAFS above 600,000 indicates strengthening business demand for goods and services, which lowers real interest rates via monetary policy feedback and supports positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are flat or negative during qualifying months, or interaction with FEDFUNDS is not significant.

mechanism_narrative: When CPIAUCSL exceeds 265 for two consecutive months, it suggests persistent inflation pressures that erode real equity returns, producing negative 20-day forward returns regardless of other signals.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive during qualifying periods, or IC > 0.15 in walk-forward analysis.
